mathlib.note: lake-manifest.json missing or without mathlib; run `lake update` in lean/

primary_endpoint.description: Strict verified success at pass@1 on the main_theorem target: original model file compiles under the pinned toolchain, its target declaration depends only on the allowed axioms, its statement is an accepted match to the audited reference, and the paper claim is established.

Strict verified success at pass@1 on the given statement: the model's completed file compiles under the pinned toolchain, contains no sorry, its main theorem depends only on the standard axioms, the theorem statement and every definition of the challenge file are unchanged as compiled declarations, and every declaration replays through the kernel. Claims that are not established are excluded.

eligibility_rules.statement_track: Paper x target has an audited reference statement (reference file present, target declaration resolved, reference statement elaborates). Open claims are included.
eligibility_rules.proof_track: Statement-track eligible AND mathematical_status is established (or refuted for disproof targets with confirmed polarity). Open/uncertain claims are excluded. Infrastructure failures are excluded from the denominator and counted separately.
eligibility_rules.compile_rate: Model returned a purported complete proof file that passed the static screen. Abstentions and infrastructure failures are excluded and counted separately.
eligibility_rules.sandwich_coverage: Paper has audited main_theorem, upper_bound and lower_bound references. Covered when all three model statements are accepted matches and every declared bridge check has review status passed.
eligibility_rules.calibration: Items with a parsed confidence estimate and a determinate outcome. Infrastructure failures are excluded and counted.

facts.note: Mixture of experts. No vendor-stated training cutoff.
Mixture of experts. Release date is from press coverage of the API launch; no Moonshot page prints it. No vendor-stated training cutoff.
Cutoff is given to the month.

model_comparison.endpoint: primary endpoint on common eligible papers (all 3 models determinate)

subgroups.note: groups with fewer than 10 papers are labelled exploratory

effort.note: Medians over all attempts in the group ("all") and over solved attempts only ("solved"); unsolved attempts usually run to their budget, so the two answer different questions.

difficulty_proxies.note: Proxies only cover the models in this run. "Smallest solver" ignores models whose parameter count is not published, so it is the smallest among open-weight solvers. A problem with models_solved = 0 has no proxy values.

generations.note: No trend is fitted and no forecast is made. Rows are comparable only when every model ran under the same protocol, budget and problem set; models released before a problem was published and models released after it are not the same experiment (see contamination).

contamination.note: A problem counts as possibly seen in training when its source was public before the model's training cutoff. "unknown" means the publication date or the cutoff is missing. A higher rate on problems published before the cutoff is a warning sign, not proof of memorisation.

reference_defects.denominator_changes: items whose reference statement is unavailable are excluded from the statement track; items whose claim is not established are excluded from the proof track (see eligibility)

caveats: Prior training contamination cannot be ruled out for public papers and public Lean formalizations.
Statement fidelity and verified proof success are separate measurements; a compile pass alone is never a success.
Equivalence classifications marked unresolved need independent expert review; automated failure to find an equivalence is not evidence of difference.
No weighted composite ranking is computed. Descriptive rankings are ordered by point estimate; only pairs listed under statistically_supported_pairs differ after Holm correction.
